balloon.image_content: Two girls are standing indoors in a living room in front of a cushioned orange-brown couch. Behind the couch is a light-colored wall with simple rectangular decorations. On both sides, there are small surfaces with potted plants. On the right side, there is also a tall vase with a plant. Each girl is holding an orange balloon by a thin string. The balloons appear similarly sized and inflated. The balloon surfaces look smooth and slightly shiny, possibly made of rubber. The girl on the right is holding her balloon a few inches above and slightly to the left side of the top of her head, with the string hanging mostly straight down. A part of the right girl’s long brown hair is lifted upward toward the balloon, with individual strands separating and spreading in different directions. Some strands point upward, others angle outward, and a few are loosely clumped, while others are more separated, creating a spiky, uneven appearance. The balloon is close to her hair but not touching it. She has a surprised expression, with wide eyes and a slightly open mouth. A small speech bubble next to her head shows symbols like “!?”. The girl on the left is also holding a balloon a few inches above and slightly to the right side of the top of her head, with the string hanging downward. Her long brown hair hangs straight down naturally over her shoulders and does not lift or separate. She is looking at the other girl with a surprised or puzzled expression, one hand resting near her hip, standing with her weight slightly shifted to one side. The girls are similar in age and height. They both wear medium-blue denim-like pants, along with casual purple sneakers. The girl on the right is wearing a long-sleeved yellow top that appears soft and fuzzy, possibly made of fleece. The girl on the left is wearing a short-sleeved yellow top that appears smoother, possibly cotton. The key difference is that the right girl’s hair lifts and spreads apart near the balloon, while the left girl’s hair remains flat.
balloon.phenomenon: The right girl’s hair stands straight up.
balloon.knowledge: Flexible materials like rubber balloons can build up static electric charge when rubbed against certain fabrics (such as fleece or wool). This charge can cause hair strands to repel each other and stand up.

bend.image_content: Two boys are standing side by side at a shared wooden sink table in a bathroom-like setting. The table has two identical sinks with metal faucets of the same shape and angle, both turned on. Clear streams of water flow downward from each faucet in narrow, steady streams. On the left, a boy is holding a transparent, slightly bluish bottle centered directly under the stream. The water falls straight down into the bottle without changing direction. The left boy leans slightly forward, watching the bottle as it fills, with a calm and focused expression. On the right side, the other boy is holding a comb close to the water stream without touching it. The comb appears to be made of plastic. The comb has evenly spaced teeth and is positioned to the side of the falling stream at about the middle height of the water flow. The stream of water on this side bends slightly sideways toward the comb, forming a gentle curve. The boys are looking closely at the bending stream with wide eyes and a slightly open mouth. They are similar in appearance, wearing light blue tops and darker blue pants that resemble soft cotton pants. Their hair is short, and their overall clothing style is similar. Behind them is a light-colored wall with a tiled or brick-like pattern. Two round mirrors are mounted above the sinks. On the left side is a rectangular cabinet, and on the right side is a rectangular window. The wooden table has a lower shelf with folded towels: two stacked on the left and one on the right. The key difference is that the water on the left falls straight, while the water on the right bends toward the nearby comb.
bend.phenomenon: The water stream bends toward the comb.
bend.knowledge: Objects made of materials like plastic or rubber can build up static electric charge when rubbed against dry hair or fabric. This charge creates an electric field that can pull on nearby water molecules, causing the stream to bend.

pepper.image_content: Two girls are sitting side by side at a wooden table in a kitchen. In front of each girl is a shallow green plate resting on a smooth wooden surface that reflects a small amount of light. Behind them is a kitchen setting with cabinets, a sink and faucet, a window, and shelves holding cups and jars. On the left side, metal utensils hang from hooks, and a kettle sits on the counter. The girl on the left is holding a spoon and lowering it toward a green plate labeled “SALT + PEPPER.” On this plate, white salt and black pepper are mixed together. Several pieces of black pepper are visibly lifted off the plate and clustered near the spoon, while many other pieces remain on the plate. Some pieces appear closer to the spoon than others, creating an uneven pattern of movement. The left girl is looking at this closely with wide eyes and a slightly open mouth. The girl on the right is also holding a spoon and lowering it toward another green plate labeled “SALT.” Her plate contains only white salt, which appears evenly spread in a thin layer and remains flat and undisturbed with no visible movement toward the spoon. The girl on the right looks surprised or puzzled. The spoons appear similar in size and shape, with smooth surfaces, and could be made of plastic. Both girls have brown hair. The left girl has a simple ponytail with a yellow hair tie, while the right girl has a ponytail with a yellow hair tie and her yellow and pink clips. They are wearing long-sleeved light blue sweatshirts that appear soft and slightly fuzzy, possibly made of fleece. Between the plates are two transparent containers: one filled with black pepper and one with white salt. The key difference is that the black pepper moves toward the spoon in front of the girl on the left, while the white salt remains still in front of the girl on the right.
pepper.phenomenon: The pepper jumps up to the spoon while the salt stays behind.
pepper.knowledge: Objects made of materials like plastic can become electrically charged when rubbed against certain fabrics. This charge can attract small, lightweight, dry particles such as pepper more easily than heavier or less responsive materials like salt.
